findings.summary: Marrowfield-ASR meets the pre-specified robustness criterion (WER increase ≤ 1.5 absolute points) at all tested noise levels (20, 10, 5 dB SNR), with increases of 0.3, 0.9, and 1.3 points respectively.
findings.scope: Tallis-Read test set with additive Ambrose-Noise (babble, street, café) at 20, 10, 5 dB SNR; WER increase over original recordings; mean over 3 seeds.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; results are descriptive means only.

findings.summary: Marrowfield-ASR shows smaller WER increases under noise than Ostrander-CTC at every tested SNR (0.3 vs 1.1 points at 20 dB, 0.9 vs 3.2 at 10 dB, 1.3 vs 6.6 at 5 dB).
findings.scope: Tallis-Read test set with additive noise at 20, 10, 5 dB SNR; WER increase over original recordings; mean over 3 seeds.
findings.caveats: No statistical test reported for the difference; only one noise collection (Ambrose-Noise) and one test set used.

findings.summary: On the original clean recordings, Marrowfield-ASR achieves a lower WER (5.8%) than both Ostrander-CTC (6.4%) and Pellucid-RNNT (6.1%), but the differences are small and no statistical test is reported.
findings.scope: Tallis-Read test set, original recordings; WER mean over 3 seeds.
findings.caveats: No statistical significance test; differences may not be reliable.

sentences.text: Marrowfield-ASR meets the pre-specified robustness criterion of a WER increase of at most 1.5 absolute points at all tested noise levels, with increases of 0.3, 0.9, and 1.3 points at 20, 10, and 5 dB SNR, respectively.
Marrowfield-ASR also shows smaller WER increases under noise than Ostrander-CTC at every tested SNR (0.3 vs 1.1 points at 20 dB, 0.9 vs 3.2 at 10 dB, and 1.3 vs 6.6 at 5 dB).

On the original clean recordings, Marrowfield-ASR achieves a lower WER (5.8%) than both Ostrander-CTC (6.4%) and Pellucid-RNNT (6.1%), though no statistical tests are reported for any of these comparisons.
